reading.body:
Profit Finder Pro Software is not a data center, and its presence in this dataset shows how a mistagged point can enter a count of AI infrastructure.

The listing is a customer relationship management and sales-tracking product sold to small businesses in roofing, solar, contracting, and insurance. Its address on file sits in the Scottsdale area of Maricopa County, Arizona, and a different company, TraVek Inc, currently occupies that suite. The point entered the dataset as an OpenStreetMap node tagged telecom=data_center. No published specification, operator, or website connects it to server infrastructure or colocation equipment.

That matters because a facility list is the base layer for counting AI capacity and the power it draws. This entry carries zero megawatts and should not be counted against the 512 MW of published capacity mapped across Arizona's four facilities with published figures. One mistagged point does not move a state total, but it shows the list is not self-verifying.

What the data does not show is how common the error is. The coordinates sit several miles from the other eight rows in the same batch, so no shared building connects them, and each appears to be an independently mistagged small business scattered across the Phoenix metro. That points to a tagging habit rather than a single mistake, though one batch cannot establish a rate. Nothing here speaks to the accuracy of the four Arizona facilities that do publish capacity.
